text.p: Gemstar Enterprises Inc Thursday said it plans to reorganize through a reverse stock split, then acquire two companies, change its name and appoint a new board of directors.

In a statement, Gemstar said the plan must be approved by shareholders, but company managment and several stockholders owning over 50 percent of the common stock have indicated they will support the deal.

Under the plan, Gemstar would change its name to C.G. Industries Inc. It would exchange one new share of C.G. Industries Inc for each five currently outstanding Gemstar shares. And it would appoint a new board.
It said it would operate as a holding company managed by John Giura and Ann Knaack. Both individuals have had numerous years of experience in corporate management, Gemstar said.

The acquisition targets are Safe Environmental Corp, a hazardous waste disposal company, and Roli Ink Corp, a maker of environmentally compatible printing inks and related products. At the present time, both companies are profitable, Gemstar said.
After the reorganization, a total 8,261,779 post-split common shares would be outstanding.
